claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus) · 2026-11-20T12:38Z · worktree issue-917 / branch issue/2901-entry-approach · plan: seat the opening rapid over the entry point at clearance; salt the toolpath cache stamp; new pins with the WCS at the centre and at a corner and with a fixture on the old line

Escalated to `effort:max` by issue-worker-high (Opus). The claim is released. The fix uncovers a safety gap that needs a new collision law. That is above `effort:high`.

**Held work** (pushed): branch `issue/2901-entry-approach`, commit `edd41f0f5`, on `origin/main` `88805e692`. No PR is open.
- `crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs`: `Toolpath::seat_approach(seed)` puts the start of the opening rapid over the end X/Y of that rapid, on the clearance plane. The `at` argument is removed.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the call no longer reads the WCS origin.
- `crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`: the salt changes from `camcraft-op-stamp-v3` to `camcraft-op-stamp-v4`.
- `crates/cl/tests/origin_approach.rs`: 8 tests pass (one new test for an opening rapid that descends).
- `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs`: 6 tests pass. They cover face, 3D finish and drill with G54 at the stock corner and at the stock centre (the same moves in the two cases). One test puts a clamp on the old origin-to-entry line: no verdict, no routed link, no `X0 Y0` block, and the posted program is the same as without the clamp. One test loads a v3 cache with the old seat (`crates/app/tests/fixtures/opening_seat_v3_cache.camproj`): it reads Stale, the post refuses it, and a regenerate opens over the entry.
- `fixture_route` (7), `golden_cl` (33, no CL golden changes), `tilt_basis_compat` (7): pass.

**The blocker (safety).** `stale_rapid_law::regenerating_the_old_cache_judges_it_under_the_new_law` fails: `the traverse at the plane is convicted now: []`.
- The fixture has a contour with the clearance plane at Z 8 under a stock top at Z 10.
- With the old seat, the invented rapid from the origin went through the stock at Z 8. The rapid law gave `RapidInStock { at: 0 }`, and the post refused the program.
- With the new seat, the opening rapid has no X/Y length. No verdict is made, and the program posts.
- The machine does not go Z first to a safe height and then over the entry. The post writes `G00 Z8`, then `G00 X.. Y..` at Z 8, from an X/Y that is not known. That traverse can go through the stock. The same is true for a fixture that is taller than the clearance plane anywhere on the path of the tool from the tool-change position.
- Thus the old seat gave a check by accident, on one line that the machine does not use. The new seat removes that check. I did not weaken the assert, as the brief orders.

**What the next worker must design.** A law for the first traverse of each operation from an unknown X/Y at the clearance plane. Examples: the clearance plane must be above the stock top (in the path frame, for 3+2 too) and above each fixture top, or the post refuses by name. The law must not give a false refusal for a stock that an earlier operation cut. Decide this before the seat lands.

**Other open items.**
- Three committed example projects read Stale under the v4 salt and do not post without a regenerate: `first_4axis_part::the_committed_project_posts_the_committed_program`, `continuous_4axis_part` (two tests), `first_router_part::first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal`. The example `.camproj` files need a regenerate and a save (the `.nc` files must not change).
- No decision file and no PR body yet. The quick gate was not run; only the suites above ran (`cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --test origin_approach`, `cargo test -j 24 --no-fail-fast -p camcraft-app --test wcs_start --test fixture_route --test golden_cl --test first_4axis_part --test continuous_4axis_part --test first_router_part --test tilt_basis_compat --test stale_rapid_law`).

Decision of the coordinator (unattended, recorded here and in the decision file of the PR). The maintainer can change it.

**The law for the first traverse of an operation.** After a tool change the machine does not know its X/Y. The post writes a Z move to the clearance plane and then an X/Y move at that plane. Thus the first traverse can cross any X/Y of the setup.

- Chosen: the clearance plane of each operation must be above the top of the stock and above the top of each fixture, in the frame of the operation (3+2 included). If it is not, the operation is refused by name before the post writes a file. The check uses the full extent of the start stock and of each fixture, because the start X/Y is not known. It replaces the check that the invented rapid from the WCS origin gave by accident.
- The test `stale_rapid_law::regenerating_the_old_cache_judges_it_under_the_new_law` keeps its meaning: the program with the clearance plane at Z 8 under a stock top at Z 10 is still refused. The cause in the diagnostic changes from the rapid at index 0 to the clearance plane. The assert changes only to name the new verdict. That change is recorded.
- A known cost: an operation that has its clearance plane under the stock top on purpose (for example in a pocket that an earlier operation cut) is refused. The message says to raise the clearance height. The in-process stock is not used here: a traverse from an X/Y that is not known can pass over material that is not cut.
- Dropped: a change of the posted order to "X/Y first at the retract height, then Z" (each NC golden changes; a larger work for its own issue). Dropped: no check at all (a collision that passes).

The three example projects that read Stale with the v4 stamp are regenerated and saved in the PR. Their `.nc` files must not change.

An `effort:max` worker of this session continues from the pushed branch `issue/2901-entry-approach` (`edd41f0f5`) when our build slot is free.
